studies.label: Supervised SAT-style essay-writing experiment, original randomized sessions

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 3, Table 1; analyzed-sample explanation in PDF p. 22, Participants

arms.name: LLM Group (ChatGPT)
arms.description: OpenAI ChatGPT was the sole permitted information resource; a supplied account was used during essay writing. Other websites and LLMs were prohibited. Initial assignment was retained across the original sessions (PDF pp. 23, 27-28).

arms.name: Search Engine Group (web search; no LLM)
arms.description: Websites were permitted but LLMs were prohibited; participants used Google with the -ai query suffix to suppress AI-enhanced answers (PDF pp. 23 and 27).

arms.name: Brain-only Group (no tools)
arms.description: Participants wrote using their own knowledge without websites, online/offline tools or LLMs (PDF pp. 23 and 27).

studies.task: Write SAT-style argumentative essays on a chosen prompt during supervised timed sessions, using the assigned ChatGPT, web-search, or no-tool condition.

ai_tool.name: OpenAI ChatGPT (participant-facing model/version not stated)
ai_tool.locator: PDF pp. 23 and 27, group restrictions and supplied account; PDF p. 151, Limitations

estimates.outcome: Essay uniqueness rated by English teachers (original sessions)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Essay uniqueness assessed by two English teachers blinded to group assignment and the existence of the experimental groups. The rubric runs from 0 (not at all) to 5 (excellent). Only the original-session observations in the session-labeled Figures 47-55 are in scope. The paper shows z-score scatterplots without an exact original-session arm mean, SD, or treatment comparison. The aggregation of the two teachers within each essay is not sufficiently specified for an independent-unit effect.

estimates.notes: Descriptive availability record for the screened original-session arm comparison. The paper prints no exact full-sample contrast statistic for this outcome. All statistical fields are therefore null; no values are read from plot positions and no topic-level results are averaged. The arm counts are the original-session analyzed participant counts printed in Table 1, not essay or rating counts. The total for these two arms is not separately printed and is not calculated. The original sessions retain the initial between-person assignment; they are not a randomized-order crossover. No outcome-specific output count or participant-level uncertainty is reported. Figures 47-55 (PDF pp. 76-84) distinguish original sessions from the optional tool-switch session. Their topic-specific observations are not extracted as subgroup effects. Pooled assessor comparisons in Figures 40-46 (PDF pp. 73-76) do not establish which production phases enter each aggregate. Differences between human teachers and the AI judge are not effects of AI assistance. No overall direction is inferred from topic-specific descriptions or rater disagreement.

estimates.outcome: Essay uniqueness scored by the AI judge (original sessions)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Essay uniqueness scored by a multi-step agentic AI judge using llama4:17b-scout-16e-instruct-q4_K_M, with multi-shot questions and a refinement loop. The judge uses the same 0-5 rubric as the teachers. Only the original-session observations in the session-labeled Figures 47-55 are in scope. This Llama model is the outcome assessor, not the participant-facing ChatGPT intervention.

estimates.outcome: Repetition and overlap of n-grams across essays (original sessions)
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: Descriptive frequency and overlap of repeated n-grams across essay pools by tool group, topic and session. The phase-identifiable analysis in Figures 79-86 uses n-grams occurring at least 3 times in an essay. This record covers the original assisted sessions only. The paper does not define or print a single arm-level overlap score, arm-level uncertainty, or overall numerical contrast. Greater repetition is interpreted as greater similarity across writers.

not_extracted.what: Procedural pilot
not_extracted.reason: The pilot described in Experimental Design (PDF p. 23) tests recording and procedures; it has fewer than the required participants and no separate reported randomized creative-output results.

not_extracted.what: S1-O2: Within-group essay cosine similarity; related PaCMAP displays
not_extracted.reason: PDF pp. 52-57, Figures 13-14 and 19: the pooled similarity display does not establish contributing sessions or original versus current tool membership. Same-writer essay pairs are not explicitly excluded. It cannot be assigned a verified across_people or after_ai question; no numerical group-average similarity or comparison uncertainty is printed. This exclusion covers both LLM-versus-Brain-only and LLM-versus-Search Engine comparisons in the screening form.

not_extracted.what: S1-O3: Named-entity distribution consistency (Cramer's V)
not_extracted.reason: PDF pp. 58-59, Figure 21: session composition and original versus current tool membership are unconfirmed. Bar values and comparison labels are figure-only; no exact arm Cramer's V values or participant-level uncertainty are supplied in text or tables. The comparison test and sampling unit are unspecified. No figure values are transcribed or assigned to an initial-session contrast. This exclusion covers both LLM-versus-Brain-only and LLM-versus-Search Engine comparisons in the screening form.

not_extracted.what: Named-entity type frequencies and total named-entity use
not_extracted.reason: PDF pp. 59-62, Figures 22-24, and PDF p. 143: entity-type counts are output text features, not idea fluency or a scalar within-arm diversity score. A text_features/other description could represent such counts, but these pooled displays and proportional descriptions do not establish the contributing sessions or original versus current tool membership. They therefore cannot be assigned to a confirmed with_ai, across_people or after_ai full-sample contrast. No separate eligible text-feature estimate is inferred.

not_extracted.what: S1-O5: Between-group KL divergence of n-gram distributions
not_extracted.reason: PDF pp. 57-58, Figure 20: separation between two group distributions does not identify which group has more internal diversity. Production-phase composition is unspecified, and no eligible phase-specific numerical contrast is printed. This exclusion covers both LLM-versus-Brain-only and LLM-versus-Search Engine comparisons in the screening form.

not_extracted.what: S1-O6: Shared ontology edges and conceptual relationships
not_extracted.reason: PDF pp. 68-71, Figures 34-38: recurring edges are described across pooled group/topic essays without establishing the contributing sessions or original/current tool membership. No phase-specific full-sample overlap statistic or uncertainty is printed; the pooled result cannot be assigned to an eligible question with confirmed AI availability. This exclusion covers both LLM-versus-Brain-only and LLM-versus-Search Engine comparisons in the screening form.

not_extracted.what: Pooled n-gram frequency displays (Figures 25-27)
not_extracted.reason: PDF pp. 62-65 and p. 132: the earlier displays do not separate sessions. Their pooled phase membership is not established. Initial-session lexical evidence is retained only through the session-separated displays in S1-O4; no pooled frequency is entered as an initial-assignment effect.

not_extracted.what: S1-O12: Essay word count
not_extracted.reason: PDF p. 55, Figure 16: pooled length means are only in the figure and have no established production-phase composition, output count, SD, SE or confidence interval. The current codebook supplies measure=length, but the unresolved phase and figure-only numbers still prevent extraction as a verified contrast. This exclusion covers both LLM-versus-Brain-only and LLM-versus-Search Engine comparisons in the screening form.

not_extracted.what: S1-O12: Essay sentence count
not_extracted.reason: PDF p. 55, Figure 16: pooled sentence-count means are only in the figure, with unconfirmed production phase and no uncertainty. Sentence counts are not idea fluency; no initial-session contrast is inferred. This exclusion covers both LLM-versus-Brain-only and LLM-versus-Search Engine comparisons in the screening form.

not_extracted.what: Essay-length dispersion
not_extracted.reason: PDF p. 55, Figure 15: the prose alternates between word length and number of words per essay, and neither the null hypothesis nor the test behind the group-labeled p-values is stated. These are not identified pairwise treatment p-values or tests of the Figure 16 mean differences; no values are read from the figure.

not_extracted.what: Former S1-O15: PaCMAP distance after the tool switch
not_extracted.reason: PDF pp. 52-53, Figure 12: same-writer, same-topic change is not diversity across people and has no established signed creativity interpretation. The optional switch analysis is not a full-sample randomized-order comparison; its Search Engine transition labels also conflict with the absence of a Search Engine follow-up in Table 1 (PDF p. 4).

not_extracted.what: Former S1-O17: Cosine distance from an AI-generated reference essay
not_extracted.reason: PDF pp. 55-56, Figures 17-18: distance to a generated reference is not a validated creativity score or diversity across human writers. Session composition is unconfirmed. The figure-only means are not transcribed; the reference-comparison prose and all-pairs formula also differ.

not_extracted.reason: PDF pp. 72-75, Figures 40-45: these assess whether an essay appears AI-assisted, not the creativity or diversity of the output.

not_extracted.what: S1-O13: Teacher-rated uniqueness after ChatGPT removal
not_extracted.reason: PDF pp. 76-84 and 122: this concerns selected LLM-to-Brain returnees in the optional later session. Comparisons use earlier unassisted essay pools or descriptive topic scores, without a concurrent never-AI unassisted control or a printed full-sample randomized after-AI contrast. The initial random assignment does not make this nonconcurrent selected-subset comparison an eligible effect. Table 1 does not establish a uniqueness-specific matched improvement.

not_extracted.what: AI-judge uniqueness after ChatGPT removal
not_extracted.reason: PDF pp. 76-84: the optional LLM-to-Brain follow-up is a selected subset with nonconcurrent comparisons. No full-sample randomized after-AI contrast or randomized-order paired uniqueness result is printed (protocol: PDF pp. 28 and 117).

not_extracted.what: S1-O14: Lexical repetition after ChatGPT removal, including comparison with earlier LLM essays
not_extracted.reason: PDF pp. 132-136 and 151: the authors describe persistence of wording among selected LLM-to-Brain returnees and compare it with earlier essay pools. There is no concurrent unassisted control or full-sample randomized after-AI contrast. The descriptive before/after pool comparison is not a paired effect from randomized condition order.

not_extracted.what: Brain-to-LLM follow-up uniqueness ratings and lexical patterns
not_extracted.reason: PDF pp. 76-84, 117 and 132-136: these optional returnees are a selected subset, and tool switching and repeat-topic choice do not supply a full-sample randomized-order contrast. No additional ai_design experiment was conducted.

not_extracted.what: Follow-up content, language/style, organization and accuracy ratings by teachers and AI judge

not_extracted.what: Separate topic-specific uniqueness and lexical comparisons
not_extracted.reason: PDF pp. 76-84 and 132-136: participants chose their essay topic. They are not turned into additional effects or averaged to construct an overall effect; the original-arm outcome availability is retained in the estimates array.

open_items: The randomized sample size, initial arm allocations and arm-specific exclusions are not printed; the analyzed counts are not treated as randomized counts (PDF pp. 22-23).
The participant-facing ChatGPT model/version and its release year are not stated (PDF pp. 23 and 27). The Llama model named for analysis/judging must not be substituted.

No exact full-sample original-session arm means, SDs, treatment differences, standardized effects or uncertainty are printed for either uniqueness assessor or the phase-identifiable lexical outcome. Participant-linked scores and repeated-output identifiers are needed; the retained rows have no usable effect statistic (PDF pp. 72-84 and 132-136).

Which sessions and original/current tool groups enter the pooled NLP and rating displays is unconfirmed. The tool-switch protocol prevents assuming that each pooled group label means a constant AI exposure (PDF pp. 28, 52-59, 68-84 and 117).
For within-group cosine similarity, exclusion of same-writer pairs and self-pairs is not established; the required distinct-person measure and independent sampling unit remain unresolved (PDF p. 57).
For named-entity consistency, exact arm Cramer's V values, the pairwise test, its sampling units, and handling of repeated essays are not supplied in text or tables (PDF pp. 58-59).

The optional later session has no concurrent never-AI unassisted control, no full-sample randomized retention contrast, and no established matched uniqueness improvement. The time elapsed for each participant is not stated; the overall scheduling period is not a follow-up delay (PDF pp. 23, 28, 117 and 122).
N-gram definitions differ between the early and later sections, and the FORETHOUGHT prose and Figure 83 caption name different reused phrases (PDF pp. 62, 132 and 134).
Figure 15 does not define the null/test or consistently identify word-length versus essay-word-count variability. Its labels cannot serve as uncertainty for Figure 16 mean differences (PDF p. 55).
The mapping of Vocabulary/Grammar in the methods to Language and Style/Accuracy in the figures is not explained; these writing-proficiency outcomes are excluded regardless (PDF pp. 72-76).

Reference-essay cosine-distance prose describes comparison to a generated essay, whereas the displayed formula uses unique vector pairs. PaCMAP switch labels also require clarification given the absence of a Search Engine follow-up (PDF pp. 4, 52-53 and 56).
The PDF identifies a project website but no explicit participant-level data or analysis-code repository (PDF p. 5). The included appendices do not provide missing creative-output statistics.
notes: Reconciled on 2026-10-11 after reading the extraction specification and current creativity codebook, both raw extractions, the comparison report, the screening map and citation record. The complete markdown conversion was read in consecutive chunks through its end, including references and Appendices A-BC. Text from every PDF page was extracted with PyMuPDF; relevant pages were read directly and Table 1 was recovered with find_tables. The two study-field differences are resolved below. The comparison report has no unmatched estimates and no differing matched estimate fields. The uniqueness slugs use A's word order; B's differently ordered slugs represent the same outcomes and arms. Agreed counts were independently checked against PDF p. 3, Table 1, and PDF pp. 22-23: analyzed people are distinguished from recruited/completed people; no randomized count is inferred. For every retained record, n_treatment and n_control are the printed original-arm analyzed counts. No two-arm total or output/rating/set count is derived. The records document original-arm outcome availability, not a numerical full-sample treatment statistic or the size of a selected topic cell. Agreed question, construct, unit and higher_is fields were checked against PDF pp. 72-77 and 132-136. Teacher and AI-judge uniqueness concern novelty of individual essays; lexical repetition concerns similarity across group/topic essay pools. Agreed outcome_with_ai and within_person fields were checked against PDF pp. 23 and 27-28: ChatGPT was available in the original LLM arm and the original group assignment was retained across sessions. Repeated essay production is not a randomized-order crossover. The six estimates are unquantified availability records with null effect statistics and no reported uncertainty. No figure coordinates, figure-only numeric labels, topic-specific results, approximate proportions or assessor differences are converted into treatment estimates. All screening outcomes and contrasts are represented by a retained record or an outcome-level exclusion; the latter applies to every contrast named there. The screening notes were also checked for outcomes omitted from its capped array. No additional eligible full-sample estimate was found. General argumentative-writing proficiency, selected optional follow-up comparisons, self-reports, memory, physiological measures and other excluded analyses remain in not_extracted. Lack of participant-level uncertainty alone is not the basis for excluding a pooled outcome: where phase is unresolved, an eligible question and AI availability cannot be established. Source entries with empty fields document measurement and scope. Every non-null numerical estimate field has exactly one source-fields entry, and every provenance quotation was checked against its cited PDF page. PDF file page numbers and printed page numbers agree at these cited locations. The same participants and comparison groups recur across the retained outcomes, so these records are dependent. Optional returnees are part of the original sample and are not added as independent arms or a new study. No other paper sharing this sample is identified in the screening form. The saved PDF SHA-256 is 9b84e8dff3e5a9eaca8d5cdcbdeef3dfb1ef32c2455eda2ed56d0079c9b45790, matching the supplied citation record identifying arXiv:2506.08872v2, revised 2025-12-31. This resolves the older screening version question for the saved file; the revision date is not printed in the PDF itself. The current codebook supplies measure=length, resolving the older screening vocabulary concern, but it does not resolve the pooled length displays' unknown production phase. Only extraction/c416.json was written. No web or API request was made.
